specification.title: A nested scope fails, and its ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails on the client
steps: Start the outer transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Write the marker `outer`, and make sure the write was sent.
Start a nested scope with the framework's nested-transaction (savepoint) API. Write the marker `inner` in it, and make sure the write was sent.
Checkpoint `inner-after-write`: report the backend PID. The runner sees the savepoint's subtransaction lock.
Arm the client-side fault (the next ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails in the driver and is not sent), then raise an application error in the nested scope.
When the fault fires, before the framework sees its error, the adapter's driver layer reports checkpoint `after-fault` (the backend PID): the runner records the fault's effect on the server.
The outer scope catches the nested scope's error.
Checkpoint `after-outer`, after the outer transaction's API has returned: report the same backend PID. The runner records whether that session is still inside a transaction.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If the API reports that the outer transaction committed, PostgreSQL committed it, with the outer scope's writes and none of the failed nested scope's writes.
When the outer transaction's API has returned, the connection that ran it is no longer inside a transaction.

execution.description: Programmatic TransactionTemplate on DataSourceTransactionManager over DriverManagerDataSource. No pool. The outer template uses the default PROPAGATION_REQUIRED. A nested scope uses PROPAGATION_NESTED. An independent inner transaction uses PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW, which opens a second physical connection. The explicit isolation case uses PlatformTransactionManager.getTransaction and commit. TX-03 is not run in this mode: DataSourceTransactionManager.doCleanupAfterCompletion releases the connection, and DriverManagerDataSource closes it, so a later unit cannot be handed that connection.

configuration.rollbackRule: TransactionTemplate default: RuntimeException and Error. A checked SQLException is rethrown as SqlUnchecked where the case needs it to leave the callback.

execution.form: Programmatic: TransactionTemplate on DataSourceTransactionManager. Outer PROPAGATION_REQUIRED. Inner PROPAGATION_NESTED, which DataSourceTransactionManager maps to a JDBC savepoint. Not PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A client-side injection in the adapter's driver layer (node-postgres, pg.Client.prototype.query): ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails without being sent, as a failed send would.
fault.injection_point: The framework's rollback of the nested scope.
fault.preconditions: The framework's statements pass through the instrumented pg module (recorded as trace_sees_framework_pg).
fault.expected_server: The savepoint is never rolled back: the nested scope's write stays in the outer transaction.
fault.expected_client: An error from the nested scope's rollback; what the framework then does is under test.

knowledge: The framework knows that its savepoint rollback failed, so it knows that the nested scope's writes may still be in the transaction.

api_outcome.basis: TransactionTemplate.execute returned normally, so the template committed
api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 TransactionTemplate.execute (org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate) obtains a transaction, runs the callback, and calls PlatformTransactionManager.commit only when the callback returns. On a RuntimeException or Error it rolls the transaction back and rethrows that same throwable. On any other throwable it rolls back and throws java.lang.reflect.UndeclaredThrowableException. If rollback throws TransactionSystemException, rollbackOnException stores the callback throwable with initApplicationException and throws the TransactionSystemException instead. DataSourceTransactionManager.doCommit calls Connection.commit and translateException wraps a SQLException as TransactionSystemException("JDBC commit failed", ex). Connection.commit is void and does not return a command tag. A normal return from execute is reported as committed. The callback's own throwable leaving execute is reported as rolled_back. Any other throwable leaving execute is reported as failed. Propagation.NESTED, Spring Framework 7.0.9: "Execute within a nested transaction if a current transaction exists, behave like REQUIRED otherwise." Its note says actual nested transactions work on DataSourceTransactionManager. DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc says nestedTransactionAllowed defaults to true and nested transactions use JDBC savepoints. Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW: "Create a new transaction, and suspend the current transaction if one exists." No custom rollback rule is installed on the template. TransactionCallback cannot throw a checked SQLException. Where a case needs that error to leave the callback, the callback rethrows it as SqlUnchecked, a RuntimeException, so the template's RuntimeException rule sees it. That wrap is application code. It is not JdbcTemplate's exception translation.

error.message: Could not roll back to JDBC savepoint: application error: the nested scope fails: injected client-side failure: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT was not sent

evaluation.reason: TX-02.1 violated: the API reported: committed; xid 9401 committed at report time (`after-outer`); outer visible: true; inner (failed scope) visible: true

preconditions.description: the write of marker "outer" had reached PostgreSQL at `outer-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "inner" had reached PostgreSQL at `inner-after-write` (a subtransaction lock, in pg_locks)
the client-side fault (client-reject) fired exactly once
the nested scope's error reached the outer scope, which handled it
the runner observed the transaction's session after the outer API returned
the withheld ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT left the savepoint live: the session was in its transaction, holding the savepoint's subtransaction lock
preconditions.detail: at `after-fault`: session "idle in transaction", backend_xid 9401; transactionid locks [9401, 9402]

invariants.detail: the API reported: committed; xid 9401 committed at report time (`after-outer`); outer visible: true; inner (failed scope) visible: true

invariants.statement: When the outer transaction's API has returned, the connection that ran it is no longer inside a transaction.
